scope: Fresh live-reference portion of the hero baseline. This records externally observable behavior and audited current live resources; it does not endorse the live site's internal architecture or any local legacy implementation.

evidenceVocabulary.observed: Measured directly in a named probe or reference frame.
evidenceVocabulary.source-confirmed: Present in an audited source, or established by exact source measurements with a cross-profile layout check.
evidenceVocabulary.inferred: Derived and compatible with evidence, but not explicitly confirmed by the source.
evidenceVocabulary.unknown: Not exposed or not measured; no precision value may be invented.

value.diagnosticEffect: The public trace query exposes progress/camera diagnostics and leaves the canonical URL and measured layout unchanged.

value.emulationQualification: Chrome 150 engine with Android 13 / Pixel 7 Chrome 149 user-agent emulation; not a physical-device performance profile

value.qualification: The live CSS-pixel boxes are an independent DOM gate. They do not resolve or waive raster failures or unknown WebGL structural landmarks.

Only exact source-to-implementation active-step layout correspondences are promoted. Glyph-sequence widths and text pixels are identity-specific; container geometry, active index, and scroll mapping remain gated.

value.policy: Only proven Vectr/Pegasoft glyph or logo pixels may be masked.
value.qualification: The flattened recording provides no pixel-precise source glyph/logo layer. Box and color/edge approximations are prohibited, so raster metrics remain unmasked.
Cross-source candidate ranking establishes target selections inside the progress-handoff tolerance. It does not establish visual acceptance.

referenceFacts.value: Exact viewport, canvas, header, logo, title, subtitle, cue, and first process-step boxes are serialized in live/dom-profiles.json.

value.behavior: Scroll updates a target progress; the renderer damps cameraProgress toward that target each frame.
value.captureConsequence: A deterministic comparison must record both target and settled camera progress; a scroll position alone is not a complete visual state.

value.glbCamera: The scene traversal selects the camera embedded in the GLB and copies its FOV when available.
value.modelRoot: The audited renderer adds the fetched scene root directly. No separate stage-three world-root rotation branch was found.
value.pointerParallax: Applied after the progress-driven camera pose; desktop pointer-floor interaction is disabled when isMobileOrTablet is true.

value.actualPredicate: The lighter asset is selected by the iOS detector, not the general mobile-or-tablet detector.

value.decision: Do not encode a blanket 'mobile loads the lighter GLB' acceptance rule.

value.reason: The raster identity is exact and the two measured live desktop profiles define stable centered DOM dimensions that cross-check against the recording landing frame.
value.qualification: Accepted capture profile. The MOV does not carry a dedicated CSS-viewport or DPR metadata field, so retain that provenance caveat.

decisionLog.value: Live source facts document what must be reproduced or deliberately challenged; they do not require copying its bundled architecture, worker topology, class names, or sequencing internals.
No local application implementation was used as measurement authority for this live manifest.
Treat browser/OS/UA and actual loaded resource as part of the capture profile. Viewport width and coarse input alone do not identify the live asset branch.
Refactor acceptance states must be externally settable as target progress plus local time/seed and must expose or await camera settlement; hidden scroll-only control is insufficient.
Use 1508×761 CSS at DPR 2 as the accepted recording capture profile based on exact raster identity and live-layout cross-check. The MOV has no dedicated CSS-viewport or DPR metadata field.

blockers.value: No fresh iOS run verifies the declared lighter GLB branch, layout, timing, or renderer behavior.
No physical Android or iOS device performance/reveal timing is available.
The live site was not freshly probed at DPR 2. This does not change the accepted recording capture profile, but it blocks a direct fresh live-versus-recording DPR-2 comparison.
Reduced-motion, WebGL-disabled, context-loss, and static-fallback states were not observed. The current audited HTML/CSS/app script contains no explicit prefers-reduced-motion token.
Live screen-space geometry for routes, arrows, contacts, subjects, and negative space requires image-based measurement at deterministic states.
Headless Chrome timing and renderer metadata are not production frame-time or memory budgets.
